summary: A bare domain-vocabulary question about an attached file ('survey number', 'subdivision number') is hijacked by a deterministic SIS database intent and answered 'No records found' / an ownership-lookup clarification, never consulting the attached file at all -- even though exactly one file is attached and it plainly contains the asked-for value.
preconditions: One session, one attached document (sis_extraction_test_en.txt, containing 'Synthetic Survey Number: 777' and 'Synthetic Sub-division Number: 777/9'), no application/survey number named anywhere in the session's real database.
reproduction: 2. Upload sis_extraction_test_en.txt (via the chat attach control).
-> Actual: 'No records found.'  Expected: '777' (read from the attached file).
4. Send: 'What subdivision number belongs to the first record?'
-> Actual: 'Which survey number or application should I look up the ownership for?' then 'Survey Ownership — No records found.'  Expected: '777/9'.
5. Control: send 'In the uploaded file, what is the synthetic survey number?' -> correctly answers '777', proving the attachment pipeline itself works; only the intent-routing gate fails.
root_cause_hypothesis: backend/services/rag.py's parse_intent() classifies any message containing the words 'survey number' / 'subdivision number' as the deterministic intents survey_detail / survey_owners, REGARDLESS of whether a concrete survey/application number is actually present in the message or in the officer's live register. Per CLAUDE.md's own documented rule in the Chat attachments section, 'targets_attachment() claims a turn only when the message names a file, uses attachment wording..., or the intent is general_query' -- so once parse_intent assigns survey_detail/survey_owners, the attachment layer never gets a chance, and the deterministic DB handler (which finds no number to look up) answers 'No records found' instead of falling through to the attachment Q&A planner or at least asking the officer to disambiguate between the uploaded file and the live register.
impact: Any officer who uploads a document and then asks about it using ordinary SIS vocabulary (survey number, subdivision number, and likely application reference, ward, block, status — the exact words the register also uses) silently gets a false 'not found' instead of an answer, with no indication that the file was ignored. This defeats the core purpose of the upload feature for the single most natural phrasing an officer would use.
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, session 68582b29-8ed4-49f0-90b0-0a17e74716b6, 2026-10-13
fix_proposed: NOT IMPLEMENTED (out of scope for this QA pass per its own restriction: 'do not modify production application code during the initial QA pass'). Candidate direction: when an attachment is active for the session, give targets_attachment() (or an equivalent earlier check) a chance to claim the turn for survey_detail/survey_owners-shaped questions that carry NO concrete number, before the deterministic DB handler commits to a 'No records found' answer.
verified_outcome: Both original repro questions now answer correctly through the real chatbot UI: "List every survey number mentioned." -> "The survey number mentioned is 777."; "What subdivision number belongs to the first record?" -> "The subdivision number mentioned is 777/9." Two root causes beyond the originally-identified routing gate were found and fixed: an LLM refusal on single-value "list" questions (fixed with a new deterministic single-entity-completion path, bypassing the LLM) and a hyphen-tokenisation mismatch blocking evidence retrieval for "subdivision" vs "Sub-division" (fixed with a lexical alias). See SIS_Upload_Bug_Fix_Report.md section 1.
remaining_known_gap: Plural-noun phrasings of the SAME question ('List survey numbers.', 'What survey numbers are mentioned?') still get a safe evidence-floor refusal in this single-document session -- a narrower, lower-severity, separate issue, not the bug's own original wording.

summary: Asking an uploaded CSV for 'all records except <status>' silently omits rows that should have been included, with no indication that the answer is incomplete. The deterministic CSV operation parser does not recognise ANY negated/inequality phrasing against a status column, so the question falls through to an ungrounded retrieval+LLM narration path, which undercounts.
preconditions: sis_survey_records_en.csv attached (12 rows: QA-CSV-001..012; rows 3 and 7 are Rejected, the other 10 are Pending or Approved).
reproduction: 2. Send: 'In sis_survey_records_en.csv, show all records except rejected.'
-> Actual: 'All records not rejected in sis_survey_records_en.csv are rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10.' (7 rows)
-> Expected: rows 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 (10 rows -- every row except the 2 Rejected ones).
-> Rows 6, 11 and 12 (all non-rejected: Approved, Approved, Pending respectively) are missing from the answer, with no caveat that the list might be partial.

direct_repro_no_ui.description: Confirmed at the function level, no UI/LLM needed: backend/services/csv_ops.py's parse_csv_question() returns None for every negated-status phrasing tried against the same 12 rows, including the EXPLICIT inequality operator.
tested_phrasings_all_returning_None: show records where synthetic_status is not rejected

root_cause_hypothesis: csv_ops._find_conditions() has a 'ne' comparator registered ('not equal', 'is not', "isn't", '!=', 'other than') but the column-anchored regex / bare-value fallback never actually binds it for these phrasings -- even the literal 'synthetic_status != rejected' is not recognised. Because parse_csv_question() returns None, attachment_qa.py's _answer_from_selected() never reaches the deterministic csv_ops.execute() path (the one CLAUDE.md documents as 'CSV questions are computed, not narrated'); the question instead falls through to the generic retrieval+LLM answer path further down the same function, which is not guaranteed complete or grounded for a row-enumeration task -- and in this live test, was wrong.
impact: An officer asking the single most natural negated filter over an uploaded table ('except rejected', 'excluding cancelled', etc.) gets a confidently-stated but silently incomplete row list. Because the architecture's own design principle is that CSV answers are supposed to be computed (never narrated) specifically to prevent this class of error, this is a gap in exactly the safeguard meant to prevent it.
evidence_source: live browser session (chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, session 68582b29-8ed4-49f0-90b0-0a17e74716b6) for the live-UI reproduction; direct Python call into backend.services.csv_ops for the no-UI confirmation, both 2026-10-13
fix_proposed: NOT IMPLEMENTED (out of scope for this QA pass). Candidate direction: extend csv_ops._find_conditions()/_COMPARATORS matching so a negator word (except/excluding/not/other than) immediately followed by a known categorical value on an implicit column (the 'bare value' fallback path, lines ~253-273) produces a 'ne' Condition instead of being silently unmatched.
verified_outcome: Exact original wording verified live: "In sis_survey_records_en.csv, show all records except rejected." -> "10 row(s) match (synthetic_status != Rejected). [sis_survey_records_en.csv, rows 1-2, 4-6, 8-12]" -- all 10 non-rejected rows, previously only 7.

summary: A direct, answerable question comparing a value that appears in two attached documents (same survey number, different status) is refused with a generic 'could not find' message instead of identifying the conflict. The system fails SAFE (no hallucinated answer) but does not deliver the comparison the master task explicitly asks for.
preconditions: Two CSVs attached in the same session: sis_survey_records_en.csv (survey 805 = Pending) and sis_survey_records_en_v2.csv (survey 805 = Rejected) -- a deliberate, ground-truth-documented conflict.
reproduction: 1. With both CSVs attached, send: 'Across sis_survey_records_en.csv and sis_survey_records_en_v2.csv, is the status of survey number 805 consistent between the two files?'
-> Actual: 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.'
-> Expected: identification of the conflict (Pending vs Rejected), or at minimum acknowledgement that survey 805 appears in both files with different values.
root_cause_hypothesis: NOT fully traced in this bounded pass. Likely candidates, in order of suspicion: (a) UPLOAD_MIN_EVIDENCE_SCORE (0.4) scored against each document's retrieved chunks individually rather than combined, so neither file alone scores high enough once the question names both filenames and a cross-document comparison verb; (b) the csv_ops path only ever reads ONE csv_doc at a time (attachment_qa.py's _answer_from_selected(): 'csv_docs = [d for d in selected if d.file_ext == ".csv"]; if len(csv_docs) == 1:' -- note the exact len==1 guard, meaning a 2-CSV selection may skip the deterministic CSV path ENTIRELY and fall through to the generic retrieval+LLM path, which then also failed to ground an answer).
impact: Phase 10's core capability (multi-document source separation and conflict detection) is not demonstrated working for a straightforward case; whether this is a retrieval-grounding gap or a hard len(csv_docs)==1 guard was not conclusively isolated in this bounded pass and needs a follow-up investigation before any fix is proposed.
evidence_source: live browser session, chatbot.html, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in, session 68582b29-8ed4-49f0-90b0-0a17e74716b6, 2026-10-13
fix_proposed: NOT PROPOSED -- root cause not conclusively isolated; a fix without confirming which of the two hypotheses (or another one) is correct would be a guess.
verified_outcome: Root cause (the len(csv_docs)==1 guard) confirmed and fixed -- with the fixture's own real header names, both files' values are shown separately with per-file citations, stating the conflict rather than refusing or merging.
remaining_known_gap: The bug's own exact original wording ("survey number 805", not the header's literal "synthetic_survey_no") still fails live -- a SEPARATE, pre-existing, explicitly out-of-scope csv_ops column-name-matching limitation documented in the regression test's own docstring, not a flaw in this fix.

summary: backend/routers/chat.py's upload_chat_file() docstring states 'A scanned / image-only PDF is recorded as no_extractable_text: there is no OCR here and never a guess at what the image said.' This is factually incorrect as of the current backend/services/doc_extract.py, which performs genuine Tesseract OCR (English and Tamil language packs both installed and confirmed working) on any PDF page with no native text layer.
reproduction: 1. Compare the two docstrings directly: backend/routers/chat.py line ~367-369 vs backend/services/doc_extract.py line ~5-9.

2. Confirmed behaviorally: uploading sis_scanned_records_en.pdf (0 chars native text, verified with pypdf) through the real UI returns extraction_status=ok, ocr_pages=[1], 292 characters of correctly-OCR'd text (UP-008/UP-009 in the test matrix).
root_cause_hypothesis: The router's docstring was written before OCR support was added to doc_extract.py and never updated.
impact: No functional impact (OCR genuinely works) -- but a maintainer or a future QA pass reading only the router's own docstring would incorrectly conclude OCR is unsupported, and the per-upload-response message an officer sees for a scanned file is driven by doc_extract.py's real behavior, not the stale docstring, so officers are not misled -- only the code comment is wrong.
fix_proposed: NOT IMPLEMENTED (out of scope: no production code was modified in this QA pass). Trivial fix: update the docstring to match doc_extract.py's own accurate description.
verified_outcome: Docstring corrected to describe the real OCR behaviour; documentation-only, no live-UI re-verification applicable.
